HON.rationale: HON is facing a severe fundamental deterioration that the market is not pricing correctly. Q1 2026 showed a dramatic earnings collapse: EPS fell 41.9% YoY to $1.29 (from $2.22), net income dropped 45.8% YoY, and operating cash flow swung deeply negative at -$650M (from +$597M a year ago). The balance sheet is deteriorating with total equity declining from $18.02B to $14.67B over the past year while total debt expanded from $27.08B to $32.11B, pushing debt-to-equity to 2.19x. Despite this earnings collapse, the stock trades at a P/E of 35.7x—near the top of its 365-day range (21.6–37.0x) and far above the ~22–24x range where it traded for most of 2025. The P/B of 10.0x is also at the top of its range (6.8–10.4x). Net margin has compressed from 15.1% to 10.9% and ROE from 31.7% to 28%. The aerospace spinoff on June 29 creates a near-term catalyst for further downside: the remaining 'Honeywell Technologies' entity will be stripped of the highest-growth, highest-margin segment, leaving behind lower-growth industrial automation and building technologies businesses that will need to justify their own valuation. The 1-for-2 reverse split is a cosmetic maneuver that does not address the fundamental deterioration. Macro headwinds are building: 10-year Treasury yields at 4.46%, 2-year yields rising to 4.19%, and CPI inflation accelerating to 4.2% suggest the Fed may need to tighten further, pressuring industrial capex. Oil prices have declined sharply (WTI from ~$104 to ~$80), which could signal weakening industrial demand. The combination of collapsing earnings, deteriorating cash flow, expanding leverage, peak valuation multiples, and a structural separation that removes the best business makes HON extremely unattractive.
